correctness.rationale: Every real vertex-aware BV input is an integral of oriented one-arm cuts with exactly its seminorm as total signed-measure mass. Orthogonal Kirchhoff arm-mode splitting yields the exact NN and DN scalar residual sums. Full Gaussian image estimates identify three uniform near-junction, bulk and reflecting-leaf regimes. The hub boundary profile exceeds all leaf and bulk maxima by a strict margin verified with rational alternating Taylor intervals; a negative one-sided derivative at the hub excludes displaced cuts in its shrinking neighborhood. Thus the hub is the unique global cut location at every sufficiently small time. The Hilbert integral equality condition and injectivity modulo constants classify all extremizers. Gaussian scaling proves the sharp coefficient. The standalone rational and numerical checker is supplementary and passed.

value.rationale: A natural compact branching diffusion graph has a BV approximation error not inferable by reflecting an interval. The exact finite-time sharp norm for all sufficiently short times, all extremizers, and its strict explicit degree law answer a motivated stability and worst-discontinuity placement question. The 3-branch hub error coefficient is rigorously larger than any reflecting-leaf profile; this is a structural graph-junction phenomenon rather than a small numeric gain or arbitrary table.
